name: hip pain overview
title: Hip pain sorted by where the patient points: anterior or groin pain inside the joint (hip osteoarthritis, labral tear), lateral pain (greater trochanter bursitis and greater trochanteric pain syndrome) and posterior buttock pain (piriformis syndrome), each with its presentation, exam, investigations and treatment in order, plus the socks question that separates lateral hip osteoarthritis from greater trochanteric pain syndrome

nodes.title: 'My hip hurts': ask WHERE
lines: TRUE hip pain (inside the joint) is usually ANTERIOR, in the GROIN
patients often point to the lateral buttock, sometimes to the buttock itself

nodes.title: ANTERIOR / GROIN: usually inside the joint
lines: also: rheumatoid or septic arthritis · osteonecrosis · iliopsoas tendinopathy

nodes.title: LATERAL
lines: hip OA can present here too: ask about SOCKS

nodes.title: Hip osteoarthritis (OA)
lines: groin, 'C' sign · socks hard

nodes.title: Labral tear
lines: all ages · commonly ACTIVE FEMALES

nodes.title: Greater trochanter bursitis
lines: very common · female > male
friction of the iliotibial band over the trochanter irritates the bursa

nodes.title: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS)
lines: chronic tendinopathy of gluteus medius + minimus, which insert on the trochanter
bursitis is only half the story

nodes.title: Piriformis syndrome
lines: muscle strain or tendinopathy ± SCIATIC nerve impingement

nodes.title: Vague groin pain
lines: • CLICKING, catching, snapping
• locking

nodes.title: Pain over the greater trochanter
lines: • CAN'T LIE ON THAT SIDE · worse weight bearing
• ± to the buttock or down the thigh to the knee
• NO swelling, redness or skin change

nodes.title: Looks like bursitis, but MORE CHRONIC and recalcitrant
lines: • insidious and slowly worse, OR a sudden flare after unaccustomed exercise, a fall, prolonged weight bearing, sporting overuse
• chronic tendinosis with acute flares of bursitis or tendinitis

nodes.title: Buttock pain
lines: • worse getting out of bed, sitting long, moving the hip
• radicular symptoms down the leg if the nerve is caught
• after buttock trauma, long sitting, anatomic anomalies

nodes.title: POINT TENDERNESS over the trochanter
lines: • highly sensitive · Ober's test +

nodes.title: SINGLE LEG STANCE test
lines: • painful within 30 s
• tender over the trochanter

nodes.title: Tender over piriformis
lines: • Pace: resisted abduction + external rotation
• Beatty: side-lying, hold the flexed knee up
• FAIR: flexion, adduction, internal rotation
• Freiberg: forced internal rotation, thigh extended

nodes.title: MR ARTHROGRAM
lines: • the imaging study of choice
• X-ray only to exclude other causes

nodes.title: A CLINICAL diagnosis
lines: • imaging not often needed
• ask about a recent increase in activity

nodes.title: Electromyography (EMG)
lines: only if the nerve is involved

nodes.title: 1 · Physio
lines: stretch the iliotibial band, strengthen the hip abductors

nodes.title: 1 · Physio + LOAD MANAGEMENT
lines: stretch the iliotibial band, STRENGTHEN the hip abductors
weight management

nodes.title: 1 · Physio
lines: stretch piriformis · range of motion · deep massage

panels.title: Lateral pain: bursitis / GTPS or hip OA?
items: bursitis / GTPS: pain on activity and lying on it · tender trochanter · GTPS: single leg stance hurts
hip OA: morning stiffness, groin pain, progressive · socks hard · internal + external rotation painful
why socks: seated = flexion + external rotation (a FABER) → hurts OA · STANDING on one leg uses gluteus medius, minimus → hurts GTPS
case: 71, lateral pain, socks easy sitting → GTPS

panels.title: Tests and the rest
items: FABER = flexion, abduction, external rotation · FADIR or FAIR = flexion, adduction, internal rotation
osteonecrosis: blood flow to bone cut, mostly the femoral head · trauma, steroids, alcohol, lupus, sickle cell, radiation
snapping hip: very common · not painful → don't worry about it · painful → treat the structure (stretch, strengthen, ?inject, ?surgery)
